evidence: src/application/PlaceOrderUseCase.ts: `export function assertExecuteRule(command: PlaceOrderCommand)` is the only definition of the customer-id rule; execute() calls it
src/application/AdvanceOrderUseCase.ts: `validateExecute(command: PlaceOrderCommand) { assertExecuteRule(command); }` calls the shared rule instead of copying it
src/application/dto.ts: toOrderDto and toStockLevelDto are the single mappers, used by every use case
All use cases inject domain ports (OrderRepository, ProductRepository, StockReservationService, IdGenerator); none uses a database or ORM directly
src/application/ListOrdersByStatusUseCase.ts uses the domain's isOrderStatus rather than its own status check
parsedVerdict.reasoning: All files serve one concern: order and stock use cases plus their DTO mappers. Every use case reaches persistence only through the domain ports OrderRepository, ProductRepository, StockReservationService and IdGenerator. No database, ORM or query client is used directly. Order and stock-level mapping is done once, in dto.ts (toOrderDto, toStockLevelDto), and every use case reuses those functions. The customer-id validation is defined once, as assertExecuteRule in PlaceOrderUseCase.ts. AdvanceOrderUseCase.validateExecute calls that function rather than copying it, which the rubric explicitly allows. Validating a PlaceOrderCommand inside AdvanceOrderUseCase is a slightly misplaced, unused helper. It is still a call to the shared definition, though, so it is neither a duplicate rule nor a bypass, and it does not split the module into unrelated concerns. ListOrdersByStatusUseCase checks status with the domain's isOrderStatus instead of writing its own check.
